UEC European Championships 2026 Men’s Elite Road Race: Our form guide

There’s no rest after the World Championships. Up next is the European Championships, which take place from 2nd-7th October 2026 in Slovenia. Defending champion Tadej Pogačar will have to miss reclaiming this jersey on home roads after his season-ending crash at the Vuelta a España, with Remco Evenepoel the favourite in his absence.

The men’s elite road race is 196.3km. Departing from Ljubljana, the peloton heads towards five laps of a 22.1km circuit around Šenčur, which features the Možjanca ascent that hits a max gradient of 15.8%.

Remco Evenepoel (Belgium)

Remco Evenepoel has won every single national and international race possible but one: the European Road Race. That’s right, with National road and TT titles, World road and TT titles, Olympic road and TT titles, and the European TT title, this weekend could see the Belgian complete an unmatched set. He has come very close before, but this is his best opportunity to get the job done.

Aside from the blip in the World Championships road race where he ended up an uncharacteristic 12th, he’s had quite the run of form recently. After his second place in the Tour de France, he won Donostia San Sebastian Klasikoa and the GP Quebec, finished fifth at the GP Montréal and claimed his fourth consecutive TT rainbow jersey.

Some big names are missing from the start list in Ljubljana, with no Tadej Pogačar, Isaac del Toro, Paul Seixas or Mathieu van der Poel, so it’s a massive opportunity. He raced to second place behind Pogačar last year on a tough French course to equal his best result in the European Championships road race having also won silver in 2021 to Italy’s Sonny Colbrelli.

  • World Championship Elite Men Individual Time-Trial
  • Grand Prix Cyclist de Quebec
  • Donostia San Sebastian Klasikoa
  • Stage 16 ITT: Tour de France
  • Stage 15: Tour de France
  • Amstel Gold Race
  • Stage 2 ITT: UAE Tour
  • GC: Volta Comunitat Valenciana
  • Stage 4: Volta Comunitat Valenciana
  • Stage 2 ITT: Volta Comunitat Valenciana
  • Trofeo Andratx-Pollença
  • Trofeo Serra Tramuntana
  • Trofeo Ses Salines

Last five results

  • 12th: World Championships Elite Men Road Race
  • 1st: World Championship Elite Men Individual Time-Trial
  • 5th: Grand Prix Cycliste de Montréal 
  • 1st: Grand Prix Cycliste de Quebec
  • 1st: Donostia San Sebastian Klasikoa

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • 2nd: 2025, 2021

Primož Roglič (Slovenia)

Slovenia might not have reigning champ Pogačar on the start line, but Primož Roglič could give his home country something to shout about. The 36-year-old might be getting to the twilight of his career, but when he’s let loose, he certainly isn’t acting like it – as evidenced by his second place at the recent Vuelta a España.

He was also particularly active during the World Championships road race, going with Van der Poel and Wout van Aert’s initial attack, and continuously working his way back to the front group of contenders once they’d been reeled in. He ended up fading in the final 20-or-so kilometres to finish 21st overall, but this course isn’t as tough as in Montreal.

Roglič has never participated in the European Championships road race before. What a time to make his debut.

Road victories this season

  • National Championships Elite Men Time Trial

Last five results

  • 21st: World Championships Elite Men Road Race
  • 2nd overall: Vuelta a España
  • 44th: Stage 21, Vuelta a España
  • 15th: Stage 20, Vuelta a España
  • 14th: Stage 19, Vuelta a España

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • N/A

Mads Pedersen (Denmark)

Mads Pedersen had a sneaky good World Championships. He kept a relatively low profile in the road race, getting dropped with around 100km to go, but suddenly appeared at the end and ended up sixth at the finish. ‘You didn’t see me,’ he acknowledged after the race.

The course in Slovenia features five laps of a 22km finishing circuit including the Možjanca climb, but the route to the finish line is a flatter parcours. Pedersen’s engine will be key over the 196.3km, and he finished Worlds as the second-best European rider, with only Van der Poel better off – and he’s skipped the European champs.

Road victories this season

  • Stage 4, Tour de France

Last five results

  • 6th: World Championships Elite Men Road Race
  • 163rd: Stage 10, Vuelta a España
  • 121st: Stage 9, Vuelta a España
  • 2nd: Stage 8, Vuelta a España
  • 87th: Stage 7, Vuelta a España

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • 6th: 2024

Giulio Ciccone (Italy)

This has been a season of almosts for Italy’s Giulio Ciccone. The 31-year-old has three recent second places on his palmarès – two from the Vuelta a Burgos and one from the GP Quebec, plus another trio of third place finishes on stages of the Tour de France.

His three ventures in Canada last month resulted in multiple top tens, and he was active towards the business end of proceedings in the World Championships road race, ending up ninth.

Like Roglič, he has never raced in the European Championships, but his Italian squad pack some options, including Christian Scaroni, Giulio Pellizzari and veteran Diego Ulissi.

  • N/A

Last five results

  • 9th: World Championships Elite Men Road Race
  • 7th: Grand Prix Cycliste de Montréal 
  • 2nd: Grand Prix Cycliste de Quebec
  • 53rd: Stage 3, Lidl Deutschland Tour
  • 48th: Stage 2, Lidl Deutschland Tour

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • N/A

Romain Grégoire (France)

Strong in the Classics this season, Romain Grégoire won the Faun Drome Classic at the beginning of the year then went on to finish fourth at Strade Bianche, De Brabantse Pijl and the Amstel Gold Race. While he couldn’t grab a stage win at the Tour de France, he did see glory on home soil with victory in the National Championships road race after a second place to Dorian Godon last year.

Since then, he’s fared well in one-day races with top ten finishes in the Bretagne Classic, GP Industria & Artigianato, Coppa Sabatini and a recent second place at the Grand Prix de Wallonie over a hilly parcours to French youngster Aubin Sparfel.

Road victories this season

  • National Championships Road Race
  • Stage 2, Tour de Suisse
  • Faun Drome Classic

Last five results

  • 2nd: Lotto Grand Prix de Wallonie
  • 11th: Trofeo Matteotti
  • 13th: Memorial Marco Pantani
  • 3rd: Coppa Sabatini
  • 10th: GP Industria & Artigianato

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • 10th: 2025

Juan Ayuso (Spain)

The Canadian block was Juan Ayuso’s return after the Tour de France, taking over a month off after finishing seventh overall in Paris. There wasn’t much to shout about in Canada, with 28th at the GP Quebec after a crash just before the line and a DNF at the GP Montréal, but he was the highest-placed Spaniard in the fight for the rainbow jersey, finishing in 13th.

Last year, Ayuso raced to sixth place on debut in the elite road race at the European Championships, and he should be competing for a podium here at least.

Road victories this season

  • GC, Volta ao Algarve
  • Stage 5, Volta ao Algarve

Last five results

  • 13th: World Championships Elite Men Road Race
  • DNF: Grand Prix Cycliste de Montréal 
  • 28th: Grand Prix Cycliste de Quebec
  • 7th overall: Tour de France
  • 151st: Stage 21, Tour de France

Best finish in European Championship Elite Road Race

  • 6th: 2025

Other riders to watch

Those aren’t the only riders who should be making their mark at the European Championships. Aside from Grégoire, France possesses a solid lineup that includes Alex Baudin, who briefly led the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes after his opening day breakaway victory, and recent Giro d’Abruzzo winner Kévin Vauquelin.

Jan Christen (Switzerland) will want to turn his fortunes around given his stage win at the Tour de Pologne ultimately led to DNFs in three of his last four races. Tour de France stage winner Marco Brenner (Germany) is also here, as is 20-year-old Vuelta a España stage winner Jakob Ormzel for Slovenia.
